anchor: The purpose of this part is to derive architectural consequences from that theory. ... How can the formal semantics of KnowledgeOS be represented by a software architecture without collapsing distinctions that the theory requires us to preserve?
statement: Part XVIII (18.1) opens the theory->architecture bridge: KnowledgeOS is a formal epistemic system K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,o_t,Gamma_t); the central architectural question is how to represent that semantics in software without collapsing required distinctions; rejects both 'a database of knowledge records' and 'a microservice per concept' as confusing abstraction levels; posits three distinct levels Semantic Theory -> Domain Model -> Implementation Model.

anchor: Theory + Architectural Constraints + Operational Requirements + Governance -> Candidate Architecture
statement: 18.2: defines T |-_arch A ('A is a candidate architecture compatible with theory T') and explicitly denies T |-_arch A => A is the unique correct architecture; multiple architectures (modular monolith, distributed system, event-sourced system, relational+immutable history, graph-oriented persistence, hybrid) may satisfy the same semantic requirements, so Theory does not imply a unique architecture; architecture is an engineering derivation from Theory+Constraints+Requirements+Governance, not a strict mathematical deduction.

anchor: S -> D -> I where S=semantic model, D=domain model, I=implementation model. The mapping is not necessarily one-to-one.
statement: 18.3: distinguishes semantic model (what entities/relations/states/meanings exist), domain model (how they become domain objects/behaviors/policies/boundaries), and implementation model (technical realization); the S->D->I mapping need not be 1:1 in either direction.

anchor: Adequate(A,Q,Gamma) should require at least SemanticPreservation, InvariantPreservation, ProvenancePreservation, HistoryPreservation, ContractPreservation... If the semantic theory requires two concepts x and y to remain distinguishable under a contract Gamma, then an architecture that irreversibly
statement: 18.4-18.5: formalizes architecture as A=<BC,Agg,VO,Ent,Cmd,Ev,Pol,Inv,Port,Adapt> and defines Adequate(A,Q,Gamma) as requiring conjunction of Semantic/Invariant/Provenance/History/Contract preservation properties; states the Architectural Distinction Principle (irreversible collapse of contractually-required-distinct x,y implies not Adequate(A,Gamma)), illustrated by Evidence≠Truth (storing only status=TRUE loses the distinction) and Decision≠Action (auto-interpreting decisions as executed actions violates the model).

anchor: BoundedContext ≠ Microservice ... Possible responsibilities are: Evidence, Epistemic, Modeling, Risk, Decision, Governance, Action

unknown_candidate.why_uncertain: This is a differently-named 7-context candidate decomposition (BC_Evidence..BC_Action) proposed in the architecture derivation chapter; may be the same evolving strategic bounded-context-map object first proposed in B0002 (BC-1..BC-7) or a distinct, later re-derivation using different names -- the file gives no explicit cross-reference.

statement: 18.6-18.7: a bounded context is primarily a semantic boundary (terminology/model/invariant/policy scope), not a deployment boundary, and may be implemented as module/package/subsystem/service/multiple services; proposes a candidate 7-context decomposition BC_Evidence, BC_Epistemic, BC_Modeling, BC_Risk, BC_Decision, BC_Governance, BC_Action with a responsibilities table, explicitly stating the theory does not prove these seven are optimal.

anchor: Candidate kernel concepts include: Identity, Context, Provenance, Time, Contract, Requirement, KnowledgeState, History, Relation, EpistemicStatus. ... A common architectural failure is to place every domain concept into a shared kernel.
statement: 18.8: proposes a small candidate semantic kernel shared across bounded contexts (Identity, Context, Provenance, Time, Contract, Requirement, KnowledgeState, History, Relation, EpistemicStatus) and warns that placing every domain concept into a shared kernel creates a 'distributed conceptual monolith'; a concept belongs in the kernel only when its semantics are genuinely shared and stable enough to justify shared ownership.

anchor: Agg=<Root,Members,Inv,Cmd,Ev> ... ValidTransition(K,c) => Inv_A(K') ... Potential aggregates include: Evidence Aggregate, Epistemic Case Aggregate, Model Aggregate, Decision Aggregate ... Proposition, Assertion, Evidence Must Not Become One Aggregate by Default

unknown_candidate.why_uncertain: This re-derives an aggregate formalism and candidate-aggregate list independently within the architecture chapter; may be a restatement/continuation of the DDD aggregate-derivation work from B0034 (aggregate-boundary-criterion, aggregate-derivation-criteria) using the same underlying invariant-ownership logic but a different symbolic notation (Agg=<Root,Members,Inv,Cmd,Ev> vs Agg=(I,O,B)), and the concrete Evidence/Epistemic-Case/Model/Decision aggregate candidates are not explicitly tied back to the earlier ten-candidate derivation.

statement: 18.9-18.12: formalizes an aggregate as Agg=<Root,Members,Inv,Cmd,Ev> with invariant predicate Inv_A(K) such that a command transition K'=delta_A(K,c) is valid only if Inv_A(K') holds (an aggregate is 'a boundary within which specified semantic invariants are guaranteed atomically'); warns against over-aggregating; lists candidate aggregates (Evidence, Epistemic Case, Model, Decision) with governed fields; and warns that Proposition≠Assertion≠Evidence means these must not default-collapse into one aggregate despite forming a pipeline Proposition->Assertion->Evaluation<-Evidence.

anchor: Candidate entities: EvidenceRecord, Proposition, Assertion, KnowledgeCase, Model, ModelVersion, Decision, Action, LearningEvent. Candidate value objects: Context, Quantity, Unit, Dimension, TimeInterval, UncertaintySpecification, AssumptionSet, Requirement, Contract, IdentitySpecification.
statement: 18.13: lists candidate DDD entities (require identity: EvidenceRecord, Proposition, Assertion, KnowledgeCase, Model, ModelVersion, Decision, Action, LearningEvent) versus candidate value objects (defined by value-equivalence: Context, Quantity, Unit, Dimension, TimeInterval, UncertaintySpecification, AssumptionSet, Requirement, Contract, IdentitySpecification); notes the classification is domain-dependent and a VO can become an entity if lifecycle/identity become domain-significant.

anchor: ObservationEvent ≢ EpistemicEvent ... IntegrationEvent ≢ DomainEvent ... ExternalMessage ≠ Knowledge ... ACL: M_E -> M_K must preserve the intended semantics
statement: 18.14-18.16: distinguishes domain/epistemic/observation/integration/audit events as non-interchangeable (an observation may occur without changing epistemic determination; a technical message is not automatically a domain fact); requires event promotion through an explicit ACL/Contract chain e_ext -> e_domain -> (Evaluation) -> Evidence -> (Epistemic Process) -> KnowledgeState, so ExternalMessage≠Knowledge; formalizes the Anti-Corruption Layer ACL:M_E->M_K as required to explicitly determine identity, meaning, provenance, temporal semantics, authority, uncertainty, transformation and loss, illustrating that silently converting 'prediction' into 'fact' is semantically invalid.

anchor: EvaluateEvidence(E,Gamma) -> Evaluation ... InferenceRule ≠ GovernancePolicy ... Repository<T> ... must not silently transform Retracted -> Deleted or Unknown -> False
statement: 18.17-18.19: defines domain services for ownerless domain operations (EvaluateEvidence(E,Gamma)->Evaluation, Estimate(M,D,EC)->EstimateResult) that must preserve assumptions/model/contract/uncertainty/provenance; distinguishes an inference Rule tuple <Premises,Conclusion,Conditions,Exceptions,Logic,Authority,Version,Provenance> from a governance Policy (InferenceRule≠GovernancePolicy, e.g. 'Decision requires Authority A' vs 'If X then Y'); requires Repository<T> to preserve identity/lifecycle semantics and never silently transform Retracted->Deleted or Unknown->False because of persistence limitations -- 'the domain must not be rewritten to fit the database.'

anchor: R_Q(K) ≠ K in general ... A query result does not itself become a determination.
statement: 18.20-18.21: a read model R_Q(K) optimized for query Q is generally ≠ K and may intentionally omit provenance/history/competing interpretations/uncertainty/rejected hypotheses -- acceptable when the query contract does not require those distinctions (an architectural form of representation independence); Command:K_t->K_{t+1} vs Query:K_t->Result are separated, and a query result (e.g. probability=0.91) does not itself constitute a determination unless the applicable epistemic contract explicitly defines that rule.

anchor: HistoryPreservation ≠ EventSourcing ... EventHistory ≠ CompleteReplayInformation
statement: 18.22-18.23: the theory's history-preservation requirement H_t⊆H_{t+1} does not imply event sourcing; possible implementations include event sourcing, immutable state versions, append-only audit structures, bitemporal persistence, hybrids. Replay(H_t,Gamma,V)->K_t under deterministic semantics may additionally require original inputs, rule/model/contract versions, context, authority, configuration and random seeds, so EventHistory≠CompleteReplayInformation unless the replay contract establishes sufficiency.

anchor: DistributedInconsistency ≠ EpistemicConflict
statement: 18.24: a distributed system's temporary State_A≠State_B from replication delay is a technical consistency condition, distinct from an epistemic contradiction where p and ¬p both hold relevant epistemic standing; eventual consistency must never be used as an excuse to erase epistemic conflict, and technical synchronization must not be read as evidence that two propositions are semantically equivalent.

anchor: LocalInvariant ≠ CrossAggregatePolicy ... Shared vocabulary does not imply shared semantics.
statement: 18.25-18.26: an invariant Inv(A,B) spanning two aggregates that cannot update atomically must be handled via domain policies/process managers/sagas/compensating actions/async validation/explicit intermediate states rather than treated as an ordinary atomic aggregate invariant (LocalInvariant≠CrossAggregatePolicy); separately, different bounded contexts may legitimately hold different models of the same vocabulary (PredictionContext's P(Y|X) vs CausalContext's P(Y|do(X))), so shared vocabulary does not imply shared semantics and the ACL must preserve the distinction.

anchor: SchemaEvolution ≠ SemanticEvolution ... V=<V_data,V_rule,V_model,V_contract,V_policy,V_schema,V_semantic> ... Canonical(R_c) ⇏ Truth(R_c)
statement: 18.27-18.29: a database schema can stay fixed while domain meaning changes (or vice versa), so SchemaEvolution≠SemanticEvolution and semantic version must be tracked independently of schema version; versioning is inherently multi-dimensional, V=<data,rule,model,contract,policy,schema,semantic> dimensions need not advance together; canonicalization (selecting R_c among contract-equivalent representations R_1≡_EC R_2≡_EC R_3) is a governance operation, and Canonical(R_c) does not imply Truth(R_c) -- it only means R_c is the authorized reference representation.

anchor: No implementation path may silently transform Evidence -> Truth ... A generic record is not a generic semantic model. ... Prediction -> Fact is generally not type-safe.
statement: 18.30-18.32: proposes candidate architecture fitness functions (semantic separation Evidence->Truth forbidden, epistemic separation Evaluation->Determination forbidden automatically, decision separation Determination->Decision forbidden automatically, execution separation Decision->Action forbidden without authorization, plus historical/provenance/type preservation); names the 'Generic Knowledge Record' anti-pattern (id/type/content/status/confidence/timestamp) where fields like confidence=0.9 hide unresolved semantic questions (confidence in what, per which model/procedure/estimand/calibration/contract); defines semantic type safety for a transformation f:T1->T2 as requiring Meaning_T1(x) to map validly into T2 under a transformation contract -- Prediction->Fact is generally not type-safe, Prediction->PredictionView may be.

anchor: DomainModel ≠ DatabaseSchema ... A system can pass Level 2 while failing Level 1. It can also pass Level 1 and Level 2 while failing Level 3.
statement: 18.33-18.34: the domain model ('what does this object mean?') and the database model ('how is this persisted?') must stay distinct -- one table may technically store several domain concepts, or one concept may need several tables/indexes/history/provenance tables/object storage -- so DomainModel≠DatabaseSchema; extends KnowledgeOS's verification discipline to architecture with three independent levels (Level 1 formal/semantic: type/invariant/contract/identity/provenance/temporal/representation-adequacy/forbidden-promotion; Level 2 computational/implementation: persistence/transitions/serialization/replay/concurrency/idempotency/transactions/API contracts/event ordering; Level 3 operational/empirical: performance/scalability/availability/latency/throughput/prediction-quality/calibration/reliability), each independently failable.

anchor: Claim -> Test -> Execution -> Evidence ... ArchitectureClaim = <Claim,Scope,Evidence,VerificationMethod,Result,Version,Provenance>
statement: 18.35-18.36: an architecture document's claim (e.g. 'the system preserves provenance') is not established merely by the presence of a provenance_id field -- it requires a Claim->Test->Execution->Evidence chain, making architectural claims themselves epistemic objects; this yields a recursive property that KnowledgeOS can represent knowledge about the correctness of its own architecture, formalized as ArchitectureClaim=<Claim,Scope,Evidence,VerificationMethod,Result,Version,Provenance>, distinguishing declared/tested/formally-proven/empirically-observed architectural properties, consistent with Claim≠Truth.

anchor: A term must not silently change meaning across bounded contexts. ... Each translation should answer: 1. What information is preserved? ... 7. What identity mapping is used?
statement: 18.37-18.38: requires a controlled ubiquitous-language vocabulary for at least 26 named terms (Observation, Information, Proposition, Assertion, Evidence, Justification, Evaluation, Determination, Knowledge State, Revision, Retraction, Conflict, Provenance, Requirement, Contract, Model, Prediction, Forecast, Causal Claim, Risk, Decision, Authorization, Action, Outcome, Learning, Drift), each term's meaning not silently changing across bounded contexts; a translation T_AB:M_A->M_B between two context models must be governed by an explicit contract and must answer seven questions (preserved information, lost information, semantic assumptions introduced, provenance preserved, authority transferred, uncertainty introduced, identity mapping used).

anchor: Loss_T = Dist(R_1) \ Dist(R_2). A transformation is contract-safe when Loss_T ∩ Dist_EC(K) = ∅. ... Zero_Arch(K,AC) means contractual architectural completeness.
statement: 18.39-18.40: formalizes the Semantic Loss Set of a transformation T:R1->R2 as Loss_T=Dist(R1)\Dist(R2), contract-safe when Loss_T∩Dist_EC(K)=∅ -- a formal foundation for deciding whether a DTO/API/projection/external integration is semantically safe; extends Knowledge Gap semantics to architecture itself, Δ_Arch(K,AC)={r∈Req_Arch(AC): ¬Sat(K,r)}, with Zero_Arch(K,AC) meaning contractual architectural completeness, not universal perfection.

anchor: A^* = arg min_A Cost(A) subject to Adequate(A,Q,Gamma) ... BoundedContext ⇏ Microservice
statement: 18.41-18.42: frames 'minimal architecture' as a constrained optimization A*=argmin_A Cost(A) s.t. Adequate(A,Q,Gamma) -- the claim 'this is the minimal architecture' has no rigorous meaning without specifying the requirement set, cost function, constraints and equivalence relation, explicitly paralleling an earlier withdrawal of universal minimality claims in the theoretical kernel; separately argues 'Microservices Are Not a Theorem' -- nothing in DDD or the KnowledgeOS theory proves BoundedContext=>Microservice; SemanticBoundary->CandidateModule does not imply SemanticBoundary->NetworkBoundary.

anchor: A_{t+1} = Delta_A(A_t,E_t,Gamma_t) ... ArchitectureRevision ≠ ArchitectureFalsity
statement: 18.43-18.44: architecture evolves as A_{t+1}=Delta_A(A_t,E_t,Gamma_t) triggered by new domain knowledge, discovered contradictions, new requirements, scalability/security findings, governance changes, operational failures or semantic clarification, and must preserve rather than overwrite prior architecture when historical reasoning is required; replacing A_t with A_{t+1} does not imply A_t=False (scope/requirements/evidence/assumptions/constraints may simply have changed), so ArchitectureRevision≠ArchitectureFalsity, explicitly mirrored to Retraction≠Falsity.

anchor: ADR = <Question,Alternatives,Evidence,Assumptions,Decision,Rationale,Constraints,Consequences,Authority,Time,Version,Provenance>
statement: 18.45: proposes representing architectural decisions with the same epistemic discipline as other KnowledgeOS objects via a 12-field Architectural Decision Record tuple ADR=<Question,Alternatives,Evidence,Assumptions,Decision,Rationale,Constraints,Consequences,Authority,Time,Version,Provenance>, making the architectural record auditable and explicitly separating the decision from the evidence supporting it.

anchor: Observation -> Evidence -> Evaluation -> Knowledge -> Model -> Prediction -> Risk -> Decision -> Authorization -> Action -> Outcome -> Observation ... The architecture must not collapse [the epistemic pipeline] into one operation such as processKnowledge().
statement: 18.46-18.47: proposes a candidate high-level architectural flow Observation->Evidence->Evaluation->Knowledge->Model->Prediction->Risk->Decision->Authorization->Action->Outcome->Observation with Governance and Provenance cross-cutting, non-linear with feedback loops (Outcome->Observation->Evaluation, NewEvidence->Revision); requires the architecture to keep every Evidence->Evaluation->Determination->Decision->Action boundary inspectable rather than collapsing them into a single processKnowledge() operation, since each transition differs in inputs/contracts/authority/failure modes/provenance/uncertainty/governance.

anchor: Lemma 18.1 — Semantic Boundary Preservation ... Theorem 18.1 — Contract-Relative Architectural Adequacy ... Theorem 18.2 [Architecture-Implementation Separation] ... BC -> {I_1,...,I_n}
statement: 18.48-18.51: Lemma 18.1 (proved): if x≠_Gamma y and architecture A irreversibly collapses x,y then ¬Adequate(A,Gamma). Theorem 18.1 (Contract-Relative Architectural Adequacy): if all contract-required semantic distinctions, invariants, provenance, history, contract semantics and implementation constraints are preserved, A is adequate for that contract (conditional, not universal, adequacy). Theorem 18.2 (Architecture-Implementation Separation): Sem(I1,Gamma)=Sem(I2,Gamma) does not imply I1=I2, i.e. multiple implementations can realize the same semantic architecture -- basis for technology evolution without domain-model change. Deployment Independence Principle: a bounded context BC may map to several deployment realizations {I1..In} and one implementation may host several BCs provided semantic boundaries/invariants stay enforceable; DeploymentTopology≠DomainTopology.

anchor: 1. Generic-record collapse ... 2. Status inflation ... 12. Architecture/governance collapse
statement: 18.52: catalogs twelve architectural failure modes to explicitly test for: generic-record collapse, status inflation, confidence inflation, event inflation, projection inflation, temporal collapse, provenance erasure, identity collapse, authority collapse, decision/action collapse, model/fact collapse, architecture/governance collapse.

anchor: XVIII-C1 — Semantic Primacy ... XVIII-C20 — Architecture Is Revisable
statement: 18.53: proposes 20 constitutional principles for KnowledgeOS architecture: C1 Semantic Primacy, C2 No Unique Architecture Claim, C3 Bounded Context Semantics, C4 Type Preservation, C5 Aggregate Invariant, C6 Evidence Separation, C7 Epistemic Separation, C8 Determination Separation, C9 Decision Separation, C10 Authorization Separation, C11 Event Typing, C12 Provenance Preservation, C13 History Preservation, C14 Representation Independence, C15 Anti-Corruption, C16 Statistical Semantics, C17 Model Separation, C18 Contract Relativity, C19 Governance Boundary, C20 Architecture Is Revisable.

anchor: Preserve the distinctions that the theory requires; collapse only what the contract permits. ... Correct KnowledgeOS = Computational Correctness + Semantic Correctness + Contractual Correctness + Historical Correctness
statement: 18.54: closing principle of Part XVIII -- 'Preserve the distinctions that the theory requires; collapse only what the contract permits'; restates the full derivation chain Theory->Semantic Model->Domain Model->Bounded Contexts->Aggregates->Invariants->Contracts->Implementation with verification circling the entire chain; concludes Correct Software≠Correct KnowledgeOS, and Correct KnowledgeOS=Computational Correctness+Semantic Correctness+Contractual Correctness+Historical Correctness, subject to declared scope and evidence; previews Part XIX (Persistence, Event History, Temporal Storage, Provenance Storage, Data Architecture).

lineage_claims.target: Part XIX — Persistence, Event History, Temporal Storage, Provenance Storage, and the KnowledgeOS Data Architecture
lineage_claims.quote: The natural next step is Part XIX — Persistence, Event History, Temporal Storage, Provenance Storage, and the KnowledgeOS Data Architecture

anchor: Persistence must preserve the semantics required by the contract. ... P(K) != K in general. The critical requirement is ... recoverability of contract-required distinctions.
statement: 19.1-19.3: opens Part XIX by reframing persistence as semantic preservation, not database design; the boundary addressed is Domain Model -> Persistence Model. Formalizes P:K->R (persistence transformation, possibly lossless/lossy/compressed/projected/normalized/denormalized/encrypted/partitioned/materialized) with P(K)≠K in general; defines Adequate_P(P,K,EC) requiring Preserve(P,Dist_EC(K)) plus Preserve of Identity/Provenance/TemporalSemantics/History/EpistemicStatus where the contract requires them, making persistence correctness a semantic property.

anchor: The database is not the KnowledgeOS ontology. ... SameStorage ⇏ SameSemanticType ... GenericStorage -> SemanticCollapse
statement: 19.4-19.6: a relational database R_t=Persist(K_t) is not itself the semantic knowledge state K_t; a query result r=Q(R_t) is generally ≠K_t and ≠Determination(K_t) unless the contract says so, preventing the error of treating database shape as domain ontology; the theory's Evidence≠Proposition≠Assertion≠Determination≠Decision≠Action chain must survive persistence even under shared storage (SameStorage⇏SameSemanticType, DifferentStorage⇏DifferentSemanticType); names the Generic Record Problem (KnowledgeRecord with id/type/content/status/confidence/timestamp) where type=prediction/status=approved/confidence=0.91 hides unresolved semantic questions -- GenericStorage->SemanticCollapse when type-specific semantics cannot be reconstructed; proposes safer Record=<Type,Identity,Payload,Semantics,Provenance,Time,Status> abstraction.

anchor: PrimaryKey ≠ DomainIdentity ... D(x,y) in {Same, Equivalent, Distinct, Unknown, Conflict}
statement: 19.7-19.10: identity distinctions (structural =, semantic ≡_sem, inquiry-relative ≈_{Q,Gamma}, provenance-sensitive ≅_prov) must be explicitly persisted since a database primary key gives only PhysicalIdentity, not automatically SemanticIdentity (PrimaryKey≠DomainIdentity); two distinct row ids cannot by themselves distinguish two assertions of the same proposition from two genuinely different entities, requiring PersistenceId, DomainIdentity, ProvenanceIdentity and SemanticEquivalence as separate concepts; reframes duplicate detection D(x,y) as a domain operation returning {Same, Equivalent, Distinct, Unknown, Conflict} rather than a boolean, since UnknownIdentity≠DistinctIdentity and StructuralDifference≠SemanticDifference.

anchor: pi = <Origin,Agent,Method,Time,Transformation,ParentObjects,RuleVersion,Context> ... Audit != Provenance ... Timestamp+User != CompleteProvenance
statement: 19.11-19.13: provenance tuple pi=<Origin,Agent,Method,Time,Transformation,ParentObjects,RuleVersion,Context> must survive persistence where required by contract -- storing only created_by/created_at (Timestamp+User) is insufficient (≠CompleteProvenance); provenance naturally forms a typed directed graph G_P=(V_P,E_P) with edges DerivedFrom/ObservedFrom/GeneratedBy/EvaluatedUsing/SupportedBy/TransformedFrom/Supersedes, where a generic parent_id may not express the relationship's meaning; audit logging ('who changed this record') answers a narrower question than provenance ('from what source/observation/transformation/model/rule/context/prior-state did this arise'), so Audit⊆PotentialProvenance in some systems but Audit≠Provenance in general.

anchor: T = <T_occurrence,T_observation,T_recording,T_publication,T_acquisition,T_decision,T_validity> ... AsOf_valid(t) != AsOf_knowledge(t)
statement: 19.14-19.16: time cannot always be one timestamp -- proposes a 7-dimension temporal tuple T=<T_occurrence,T_observation,T_recording,T_publication,T_acquisition,T_decision,T_validity>, illustrated by an event occurring Jan1 but being learned Jan10 (T_occurrence≠T_knowledge, both must be preservable); recommends bitemporal storage x=<Content,VT,TT> (valid time vs transaction/knowledge time) enabling AsOf_valid(t)≠AsOf_knowledge(t) queries, but warns bitemporal storage (two time dimensions) is not automatically a complete temporal ontology -- additional dimensions (occurrence/publication/observation/decision/execution/model-version/contract-validity time) may still be needed depending on the contract.

anchor: Persistence should therefore not simply overwrite status=established with status=retracted ... DELETE != RETRACT ... SoftDelete != Retraction
statement: 19.17-19.23: Current(K_t) must be distinguished from History(K_t) -- overwriting status fields destroys required reconstruction, so K_t->K_{t+1} must remain reconstructible; append-only history H_{t+1}=H_t∪{e_{t+1}} supports this but AppendOnly≠AutomaticallyCorrect (a log can still hold incorrect/duplicate/misordered/invalid events, so history preservation does not replace semantic validation); event sourcing K_t=Replay(E_1..E_t) is a candidate implementation strategy, not a theorem, and introduces schema-stability/versioning/deterministic-replay/ordering/migration/idempotency requirements; replaying event E_7 under a changed RuleVersion (3 vs 4) can legitimately produce K'_t≠K_t, so reproducible historical replay needs Replay(H_t,V_rules,V_models,V_contracts,V_schemas) not just Replay(H_t); a system must represent both Determined(p,t1) and Retracted(p,t2) without contradiction since each is a per-time status statement; DELETE≠RETRACT (deletion destroys the representation, retraction changes epistemic standing while preserving historical existence), and a common 'deleted_at' SoftDelete implementation is not automatically a Retraction model.

anchor: Conflict = <Claims,Evidence,Context,Time,ResolutionStatus,Provenance> ... DatabaseConflict != EpistemicConflict ... r = <Type,Source,Target,Context,Time,Provenance,Status>
statement: 19.24-19.26: epistemic conflicts (p supported by e1, ¬p supported by e2) must be preserved via a Conflict=<Claims,Evidence,Context,Time,ResolutionStatus,Provenance> tuple with a legitimate Status(p)=Conflicted state, rather than resolved by picking one row; two contradictory database rows are not automatically an epistemic conflict (could be historical change, multiple observations/contexts, corruption, or concurrent updates) -- DatabaseConflict≠EpistemicConflict; relations are first-class semantic objects r=<Type,Source,Target,Context,Time,Provenance,Status>, since a bare source_id/target_id edge cannot specify whether A->B means supports/contradicts/depends-on/derives-from/describes/causes/supersedes.

anchor: Multiple physical stores must not create multiple incompatible semantic truths. ... Loss_Q = Dist(K)\Dist(R_Q(K)). This is acceptable when Loss_Q ∩ Dist_EC(K) = ∅.
statement: 19.27-19.31: a graph database is a persistence technology, not an epistemology (Graph≠KnowledgeState, may omit contracts/uncertainty/temporal/assumptions/authority/revision semantics); relational storage is often equally suitable, so the theory implies neither KnowledgeGraph>RelationalDatabase nor the reverse -- choice is contract/workload-dependent; KnowledgeOS may legitimately use polyglot persistence (relational for aggregates, object store for artifacts, graph store for traversal, search index, event store, vector index) but must define a canonical semantic state K with projections R1(K),R2(K),R3(K) and an authority rule for which representation answers which semantic question (a vector index may answer similarity, not determination -- SimilarityResult≠Determination); formalizes projection Loss_Q=Dist(K)\Dist(R_Q(K)) as acceptable exactly when Loss_Q∩Dist_EC(K)=∅, giving a rigorous read-model design test.

anchor: RetrievedDocument != Evidence ... EmbeddingSimilarity != SemanticIdentity
statement: 19.32-19.33: search/retrieval results Documents={d1..dn} are retrieval results, becoming evidence only after an epistemic process determines they satisfy an evidence contract (RetrievedDocument≠Evidence, SimilarityScore≠EvidenceStrength), flagged as especially important for AI-assisted retrieval; an embedding similarity score sim(x,y)=0.92 establishes only that the chosen similarity model assigns a high score, not x≡_sem y nor Truth(x)=Truth(y) (EmbeddingSimilarity≠SemanticIdentity) unless a separately validated contract establishes such equivalence.

anchor: AI generation is provenance. It is not automatically authority. ... p should preserve DerivedFrom(p,s,m). The extraction result is not identical to the original observation.
statement: 19.34-19.35: AI-generated outputs (hypotheses, summaries, classifications, extracted propositions/relations/entities/evidence) must preserve GeneratedBy=AIModel_v as distinguishable from ObservedBy=HumanInstrument or PublishedBy=ExternalAuthority -- AI generation is provenance, not automatically authority; an extraction such as 'Company X acquired Company Y' from source s via extraction method m yields proposition p that must preserve DerivedFrom(p,s,m), since the extraction result is not identical to the original observation, permitting later correction when the extraction model was wrong.

anchor: U = <Type,Quantity,Scale,Model,Procedure,Assumptions,Population,Time,Calibration,Provenance> ... Uncertainty != SingleNumber ... EqualOutput != EqualModelMeaning
statement: 19.36-19.40: uncertainty must not be stored as a bare confidence number; proposes U=<Type,Quantity,Scale,Model,Procedure,Assumptions,Population,Time,Calibration,Provenance> across types (probability, interval, variance, SE, posterior, prediction interval, qualitative, ambiguity, incomplete knowledge) -- Uncertainty≠SingleNumber; a statistical estimate theta-hat needs <Estimand,Estimator,Estimate,Population,Sample,SamplingDesign,Model,Assumptions,Uncertainty,Procedure,Version,Provenance> since a bare number like 4.72 does not specify mean/median/coefficient/odds-ratio/hazard-ratio/effect/probability (NumericValue≠StatisticalMeaning); a model prediction y=f-hat(x) needs Prediction=<Input,Output,ModelId,ModelVersion,ParameterSet,Assumptions,Time,Contract,Uncertainty,Provenance>; two models M1≠M2 giving numerically equal outputs (0.73=0.73) need not share assumptions/training/calibration/causal-interpretation/uncertainty/validity-scope, so EqualOutput≠EqualModelMeaning.

anchor: Det(K,p,EC) cannot be fully understood if EC is unavailable when the determination is reconstructed. ... V_x = <V_schema,V_semantic,V_contract,V_rule,V_model,V_policy,V_identity>
statement: 19.41-19.42: because KnowledgeOS is contract-relative, a historical determination Det(K,p,EC) needs a reference to ContractVersion plus rule/policy/model/schema/identity-policy versions to remain reconstructible; proposes a per-object version vector V_x=<V_schema,V_semantic,V_contract,V_rule,V_model,V_policy,V_identity> where not every object needs every component, making explicit that semantic reproducibility can depend on several independent version dimensions.

anchor: A valid migration should satisfy Sem(R_1) ≡_Gamma Sem(R_2) ... RetentionContract ... HashEquality != SemanticIdentity ... ContentIdentity != DomainIdentity ... ImmutableRepresentation != ImmutableMeaning
statement: 19.43-19.48: distinguishes technical schema migration (Schema1->Schema2 preserving semantics) from semantic migration (Meaning1->Meaning2, which is domain evolution not mere migration); a migration is lossless under contract EC iff Loss_M∩Dist_EC(K)=∅, and UnknownLoss is itself a risk; legal/security/retention deletion requirements can conflict with historical reconstruction, requiring an explicit RetentionContract (what may be deleted/must remain/may be anonymized/what provenance and reconstruction survive) since DeletionPolicy≠EpistemicPolicy; cryptographic hash equality h(x)=h(y) establishes hashed-representation equality only, not semantic identity (HashEquality≠SemanticIdentity; semantically equivalent x≡_sem y can have h(x)≠h(y)); content-addressable id=h(content) is useful for immutable artifacts but ContentIdentity≠DomainIdentity; 'immutable' has at least 5 distinct referents (bytes/records/facts/events/claims) so ImmutableRepresentation≠ImmutableMeaning (a document can stay immutable while its interpretation changes).

anchor: delta(delta(K,o_1),o_2) != delta(delta(K,o_2),o_1) ... Idempotency is an operation property, not a universal property ... DuplicateMessage != DuplicateDomainFact ... WallClockOrder != CausalOrder
statement: 19.49-19.53: concurrent operations o1∥o2 may be commutative, conflicting, causally ordered, independently applicable, or reconciliation-requiring, and in general delta(delta(K,o1),o2)≠delta(delta(K,o2),o1) so order can be semantically relevant; idempotency (delta(delta(K,o),o)=delta(K,o)) must be defined per operation (reading is naturally idempotent, recording an observation or creating an assertion generally is not, retracting the same assertion may be) -- an operation property, not a universal KnowledgeOS property; distributed duplicate delivery of the same technical event e,e does not imply TwoDomainEvents, requiring an identity/deduplication contract (EventId, SourceId, SequenceNumber, Provenance, DomainIdentity) since DuplicateMessage≠DuplicateDomainFact; e1<e2 must not be assumed merely from timestamp(e1)<timestamp(e2) (WallClockOrder≠CausalOrder) -- ordering may require source sequence/logical clocks/causal dependencies/transaction order/explicit temporal semantics; logical 'happened-before' clocks (e1->e2) establish ordering without claiming physical time.

anchor: DatabaseTransaction != DomainAggregate ... AtomicCommit != EpistemicValidity ... TechnicalConsistencyPolicy != EpistemicConflictPolicy ... CachedResult != CurrentKnowledge ... FreshnessContract(V,Q,Gamma)
statement: 19.54-19.58: a database transaction's Atomicity guarantee and an aggregate's DomainInvariant guarantee are related but not identical -- a transaction updating ten unrelated concepts does not thereby make them one aggregate (DatabaseTransaction≠DomainAggregate); successfully committing a distributed transaction gives AtomicCommit, not EpistemicValidity (e.g. committing evidence.status=accepted does not establish epistemic sufficiency); replication-delay divergence K_A(t)≠K_B(t) must not be read as KnowledgeConflict, and conversely genuine evidence conflicts must not be silently overwritten by eventual synchronization (TechnicalConsistencyPolicy≠EpistemicConflictPolicy); a cache C_t=Cache(K_{t-Delta}) may be stale, so CachedResult≠CurrentKnowledge unless a freshness contract Fresh(C,Q,Gamma,t) establishes equivalence; likewise a materialized view V_t=f(K_t) requires a FreshnessContract(V,Q,Gamma) once K changes.

anchor: LineageGraph rather than merely created_from_id ... Quality(Data) should not automatically be reduced to QualityScore in [0,1] ... NULL semantics must be domain-defined.
statement: 19.59-19.64: proposes preserving a full lineage chain Source->Document->Extraction->Proposition->EvidenceEvaluation->Determination->Decision as a semantically-typed LineageGraph rather than a bare created_from_id; data quality (completeness, accuracy, consistency, timeliness, validity, uniqueness, provenance completeness, semantic adequacy) should not collapse into one QualityScore∈[0,1] without explicit dimensions/calibration, since a dataset can be complete-but-inaccurate, accurate-but-incomplete, etc.; persistence must distinguish Missing from Zero from False from Unknown from NotApplicable (a NULL temperature does not reveal which applies) -- NULL is a technical representation and must not automatically become 'Unknown' without an explicit MissingReason mapping {NotMeasured, Unavailable, Withheld, Unknown, NotApplicable}; database constraints (uniqueness, FKs, non-null, checks) give ReferentialIntegrity, not EpistemicIntegrity -- a perfectly normalized DB can store a false proposition and a messy DB can hold valid evidence; normalization/denormalization are neither inherently epistemically superior, the choice depends on Performance+Consistency+QueryRequirements+History+SemanticPreservation.

anchor: Shared infrastructure should not be confused with shared domain semantics. ... SharedKernel != SharedDatabase ... DomainContract > PersistenceSchema ... View_A(K) != K
statement: 19.65-19.72: a database table shared directly by two bounded contexts (BC_A -> SharedTable <- BC_B) risks each context interpreting the same field differently -- SharedStorage->SharedMeaning without actual semantic agreement, so shared infrastructure ≠ shared domain semantics; a DDD shared kernel (intentional semantic agreement) is not the same as a shared database (merely technical coupling) -- SharedKernel≠SharedDatabase; every canonical concept should have an explicit domain-semantics owner (e.g. EvidenceContext owns evidence, DecisionContext owns decision; a decision context should not directly rewrite evidence semantics), with persistence ownership following domain ownership (SemanticOwnership->PersistenceBoundary); APIs should expose domain operations (retrieveEvidence, evaluateProposition, retractAssertion, determine) rather than raw persistence structures (DomainContract>PersistenceSchema); security metadata (access authority, classification, confidentiality, consent, legal basis, integrity status) affects Visibility(K,Gamma) but AccessRestriction≠NonExistence -- an object unavailable to participant A may still exist, giving participant-relative Knowledge Views View_A(K)≠K, View_A(K)≠View_B(K) possibly without contradiction (authorization/confidentiality/scope/purpose-limitation); provenance graphs can conflict with privacy (revealing identities/sources/relationships/access patterns), so ProvenancePreservation is itself subject to a PrivacyContract.

anchor: EC, DC, PC, RC, SC, TC, GC ... Adequate_P(P,C) ... Delta_P = {r in Req_P(PC): not Sat(P,r)} ... Zero_P(P,PC) iff Delta_P = empty
statement: 19.73-19.76: reframes persistence design as satisfying a compatible intersection of multiple contracts C={EC,DC,PC,RC,SC,TC,GC} (Epistemic/Decision/Persistence/Retention/Security/Temporal/Governance Contracts), giving Adequate_P(P,C) rather than a single database property; defines the Persistence Knowledge Gap Delta_P={r∈Req_P(PC): ¬Sat(P,r)} (e.g. unreconstructible provenance/history/identity/temporal-dimensions/model-versions) and Persistence Zero Zero_P(P,PC) iff Delta_P=∅, meaning satisfaction of explicit persistence requirements under PC -- explicitly Zero_P≠Truth and Zero_P≠UniversalCompleteness; defines a persistence repair operator Repair_P:(P,Delta_P)->P' reducing |Delta_P| via adding provenance/temporal fields/restoring events/versioning rules/repairing identity/rebuilding projections/migrating schema, noting Repair≠GuaranteedTruth.

anchor: Theorem 19.1 — Contractual Reconstruction ... Theorem 19.2 [Projection Adequacy] ... Theorem 19.3 [History Preservation] ... Theorem 19.4 [Semantic Migration]
statement: 19.77-19.80: Theorem 19.1 (Contractual Reconstruction) -- if persistence preserves all EC-required distinctions/provenance/temporal/version/history information, a reconstruction function Rec_EC exists with Rec_EC(P(K_t))≡_EC K_t (semantic equivalence, not structural identity -- Rec(P(K))=K is 'unnecessarily strong'); Theorem 19.2 (Projection Adequacy) -- a query-Q projection R_Q(K) is contractually adequate for Q iff Loss_Q∩Dist_EC(Q)=∅, i.e. a projection need only preserve what its query contract requires; Theorem 19.3 (History Preservation) -- if persistence stores a transition o with all semantic replay dependencies, Replay(H_t,V_t)≡_Gamma K_t under the applicable replay contract; Theorem 19.4 (Semantic Migration) -- a migration M:R1->R2 is semantically preserving iff Sem(R1)≡_Gamma Sem(R2) for all required contracts, otherwise it represents semantic change or loss, so SchemaMigration must be evaluated separately from SemanticMigration.

anchor: p, not-p does not entail q [persistence non-explosion] ... CorruptionDetected as a system event/evidence object ... Backup != CompleteKnowledgeHistory ... SystemRecovery != KnowledgeRecovery
statement: 19.81-19.84: a persistence-level inconsistency producing p and ¬p must be isolated by the architecture rather than licensing inference of arbitrary q (p,¬p⊬q -- Persistence Non-Explosion Principle), turning persistence corruption into an object of diagnosis rather than a license for arbitrary conclusions; a corrupted record is itself information and should be preserved as a CorruptionDetected system event/evidence object (affected object, detection method, time, integrity evidence, suspected cause, scope, repair status) to prevent silent history rewriting; a backup provides a data copy but not necessarily semantic context/rule-versions/model-versions/contracts/provenance/deployment-configuration (Backup≠CompleteKnowledgeHistory); technical disaster recovery ('can the system come back online?') and knowledge recovery ('can the required semantic state and history be reconstructed?') are distinct (SystemRecovery≠KnowledgeRecovery) -- a system can be operational while having lost epistemically important history.

anchor: Level 1 Semantic Verification ... Level 2 Computational Verification ... Level 3 Operational Verification ... F1 — Provenance preservation ... F10 — Authorization safety
statement: 19.85-19.86: applies the three-level KnowledgeOS verification discipline to data architecture (Level 1 semantic: type/identity/provenance/temporal/epistemic-status/contract-refs/relation-types/uncertainty; Level 2 computational: transitions/transaction-boundaries/replay/migration/concurrency/idempotency/ordering/projection-rebuild; Level 3 operational: performance/capacity/recovery-time/throughput/replication/availability/backup-restore/latency), noting a successful benchmark does not prove semantic correctness; proposes 10 candidate automated fitness functions F1 Provenance preservation, F2 History preservation, F3 Type preservation, F4 Temporal preservation, F5 Version preservation, F6 Identity preservation, F7 Projection safety, F8 Retraction safety, F9 Model-result safety, F10 Authorization safety.

anchor: D_canonical, D_history, D_provenance, D_source, D_projection, D_search, D_analytics ... Derived ⇏ Disposable ... ImmutableSource != TrueSource
statement: 19.87-19.90: proposes seven conceptual (not necessarily physically-separate) persistence-layer responsibilities D_canonical, D_history, D_provenance, D_source, D_projection, D_search, D_analytics; distinguishes CanonicalData from DerivedData (Derived=f(Canonical), requiring an identifiable canonical source) and notes an unregenerable derived projection may itself become canonical under a separate contract -- Derived⇏Disposable, status must be explicit; original source artifacts (documents, PDFs, images, datasets, logs, API responses, measurements) should be preserved so extracted objects can reference them via DerivedFrom for later re-evaluation; an immutable source artifact preserves 'what was received', not truthfulness -- ImmutableSource≠TrueSource, authority is a separate property.

anchor: Because source artifacts and provenance are preserved, KnowledgeOS can revisit previous determinations. ... Memory = <Current,Historical,Provenance,Semantic,Operational> ... SemanticState' ≡_EC SemanticState
statement: 19.91-19.94: because sources/provenance persist, a corrected Extraction_v2 can drive a revision Determination_v1->Determination_v2 while history remains intact, yielding the architectural pairing Reproducibility+Revisability; frames persistence as a multi-layer memory Memory=<Current,Historical,Provenance,Semantic,Operational>, arguing a system storing only current values has a 'very weak memory model'; formalizes the persistence boundary as SemanticState -Encode-> PersistentRepresentation -Decode-> SemanticState' with the required property SemanticState'≡_EC SemanticState (not structural Representation'=Representation, and not necessarily literal SemanticState'=SemanticState if the system legitimately evolved) -- the contract determines which equivalence matters; states the Data Architecture Principle: 'Persist what must be remembered; derive what can be reconstructed; preserve the provenance of what is derived; and never mistake a representation for the knowledge itself.'

anchor: XIX-C1 — Persistence Is Representation ... XIX-C20 — No Semantic Inflation
statement: 19.95: 20 constitutional statements for KnowledgeOS persistence: C1 Persistence Is Representation, C2 Contractual Adequacy, C3 Semantic Preservation, C4 Identity Separation, C5 Provenance Preservation, C6 Temporal Preservation, C7 History Preservation, C8 Retraction Separation, C9 Conflict Preservation, C10 Relation Typing, C11 Projection Separation, C12 Retrieval Separation, C13 Similarity Separation, C14 Model Provenance, C15 Statistical Provenance, C16 Version Preservation, C17 Migration Safety, C18 Distributed Consistency Separation, C19 Recovery Semantics, C20 No Semantic Inflation.

anchor: Data Storage != Knowledge Storage ... Knowledge Storage = Data + Semantics + Provenance + Time + History + Contracts + Identity ... Part XX — Query Semantics, Retrieval, Search, Knowledge Graph Traversal, RAG ...
statement: 19.96: closing formula Persistence Correctness = Semantic Preservation + Historical Preservation + Provenance Preservation + Temporal Preservation + Contractual Preservation (subject to declared scope); the database becomes part of the memory architecture only once meaning/origin/validity-time/contract/change-history/recoverable-distinctions are established, giving Data Storage≠Knowledge Storage and Knowledge Storage=Data+Semantics+Provenance+Time+History+Contracts+Identity; establishes foundation for Persistence->APIs->Queries->Retrieval->Inference and explicitly previews Part XX (Query Semantics, Retrieval, Search, Knowledge Graph Traversal, RAG, Semantic Search, and the boundary between retrieval and inference) with the central next distinction 'retrieval ≠ evidence ≠ inference'.

lineage_claims.target: Part XX — Query Semantics, Retrieval, Search, Knowledge Graph Traversal, RAG, Semantic Search, and the Boundary Between Retrieval and Inference
lineage_claims.quote: That is the subject of Part XX — Query Semantics, Retrieval, Search, Knowledge Graph Traversal, RAG, Semantic Search, and the Boundary Between Retrieval and Inference.

anchor: Retrieval != Evidence != Inference != Determination. And therefore: Retrieved Text != Truth.
statement: 20.1: opens Part XX at the boundary KnowledgeState->Query->Retrieval->Interpretation->Inference, arguing that the apparently simple AI action 'search the knowledge and answer the question' is architecturally at least 11 distinct operations (query interpretation, candidate retrieval, filtering, ranking, evidence selection, context construction, inference, answer generation, confidence estimation, provenance construction, determination); states the foundational boxed distinction Retrieval≠Evidence≠Inference≠Determination and Retrieved Text≠Truth.

anchor: Retrieval(K,Q) ⇏ Truth(Q). ... Q_c != Q_s in general. ... Q = <Target,Predicate,Scope,Context,Purpose,Time,Contract>
statement: 20.2-20.4: formalizes retrieval R(K,Q)={x1..xn} answering only 'which objects were selected', not 'which proposition is true' (Retrieval(K,Q)⇏Truth(Q)); distinguishes a semantic inquiry Q_s from its computational encoding Q_c=Encode(Q_s), generally Q_c≠Q_s since encoding may be lossy (e.g. status='approved' does not capture contract version/evidence requirements/authority/temporal scope/conflict state/provenance); proposes a 7-field query tuple Q=<Target,Predicate,Scope,Context,Purpose,Time,Contract>, arguing relevance cannot be rigorously evaluated without it.

anchor: s(x,Q) != TruthScore(x). ... Relevance != Truth != EvidenceStrength != Determination. ... HighRecall ⇏ HighTruthfulness.
statement: 20.5-20.9: defines Ret:K×Q×Γ->P(X) with per-object scores s(x_i,Q)≠TruthScore(x); Relevance(d,Q)=0.97 implies neither Truth(d)=1 nor EvidenceStrength(d,Q)=0.97 nor Determined(Q), giving the boxed Relevance≠Truth≠EvidenceStrength≠Determination; a ranking function Rank:X×Q->R (lexical/BM25/vector/hybrid/graph/learned) is itself a model M_rank whose output must not be silently promoted to epistemic standing; Precision/Recall are retrieval metrics that do not establish truth (HighRecall⇏HighTruthfulness, HighPrecision⇏Truth); even retrieval evaluation needs a declared reference relevance set Rel*(Q) which is itself context/purpose/temporal/participant/contract-dependent.

anchor: SameQuery ⇏ SameResult [without retrieval provenance]. ... R_{t_1}(Q) != R_{t_2}(Q) ... R_A(Q) != R_B(Q) may be legitimate.
statement: 20.10-20.14: search is Query->CandidateGeneration->Ranking->Filtering->Presentation, and the displayed result requires retrieval provenance RP=<Query,Retriever,RetrieverVersion,Index,Timestamp,Filters,Ranking,Candidates,SelectionRule> (and RR=<Object,Score,Rank,RP>) since without it SameQuery⇏SameResult; retrieval is temporal (R_{t1}(Q)≠R_{t2}(Q) from new/retracted documents, changed ranking/index/permissions/embeddings/knowledge), motivating snapshot retrieval R(Q,K_t) vs R(Q,K_now) for historical decisions/audits/experiments/legal review/reproducibility; because participants may have different knowledge views View_A(K), retrieval may legitimately differ R_A(Q)≠R_B(Q) reflecting authorization/context rather than inconsistency.

anchor: LexicalMatch != SemanticEquivalence. ... sim(x,y) ≈ 1 ⇒ x ≡_sem y [is generally invalid]. ... RetrievalModelDrift.
statement: 20.15-20.19: lexical search Ret_L(Q,D) preserves exact terminology/identifiers/legal-phrases/version-numbers but LexicalMatch≠SemanticEquivalence; semantic search uses an embedding phi and similarity sim(phi(x),phi(q)) that is model-relative -- sim(x,q)=0.91 means only that the chosen representation assigns high similarity, not x≡_sem q; names the Embedding Equivalence Fallacy sim(x,y)≈1⇒x≡_sem y as generally invalid since embeddings compress information and different concepts can map to nearby regions (EmbeddingSpace is a retrieval representation, not a complete semantic ontology); if embedding model E1 is replaced by E2, phi_E1(x) may differ substantially from phi_E2(x), producing RetrievalModelDrift, so embedding versions must be part of retrieval provenance; recommends hybrid retrieval R=R_lexical∪R_semantic∪R_structured∪R_graph combining methods that preserve different distinctions.

anchor: DatabasePrecision != EpistemicCorrectness. ... Path(G,A,C) ⇏ Infer(A,C,Gamma). ... Supports(A,B) and Supports(B,C) [does not imply] Supports(A,C).
statement: 20.20-20.24: a structured query (SELECT x such that Status(x)=Established) can be precise but only as correct as the stored status and its defining contract (DatabasePrecision≠EpistemicCorrectness); for a typed knowledge graph G=(V,E), a path A->B->C does not establish A->C (path composition requires explicit semantic rules), formalized as the 'fundamental KnowledgeOS principle' Path(G,A,C)⇏Infer(A,C,Gamma); relation composition must be type-specific -- Supports(A,B)∧Supports(B,C) does not imply Supports(A,C), and DependsOn transitivity holds only if the relation contract defines it; graph traversal answers structural reachability, not epistemic justification, so Traversal≠Inference (a traversal may supply premises for a separately-evaluated inference).

anchor: GeneratedAnswer != RetrievedEvidence. ... RAG != TruthGuarantee. ... CitationPresence != CitationValidity.
statement: 20.25-20.30: retrieval is framed as candidate generation (Retrieval: Question->CandidateInformation, narrowing not establishing the answer), especially relevant for AI systems; RAG is Q->R(K,Q)->Context(R)->Generator(Q,R)->Answer with GeneratedAnswer≠RetrievedEvidence and GeneratedAnswer≠Determination unless separately validated; rejects 'grounded because retrieved' as RAG≠TruthGuarantee since documents themselves may be wrong/outdated/contradictory/incomplete/irrelevant/generated/unauthorized; a governed RAG process should preserve the full chain Q->Retriever->Documents->Chunks->Claims->Inference->Answer with each transformation inspectable (Answer->Claim->SourceChunk->SourceDocument = answer provenance); a citation establishes Answer->Source but not Source⊨Answer, so CitationPresence≠CitationValidity, requiring a separate Supports(d,p,Gamma) evaluation and pipeline Retrieve->EvaluateSupport->UseAsEvidence.

anchor: Selected != True. ... Distinct(d1,d2,d3) [does not imply] Independent(d1,d2,d3). ... RetrievedSample != RepresentativeSample ... Ranking -> Exposure -> HumanSelection -> EvidenceUse -> Knowledge.
statement: 20.31-20.36: evidence selection E=Select(R,Q,Gamma) (by authority/relevance/recency/provenance/independence/methodological-quality/contradiction/completeness) yields Selected≠True, only 'selected as potentially useful under contract'; documents sharing one ultimate source (d1,d2,d3<-s) are Distinct but not thereby Independent (illustrated by ten sites repeating one press release), so naive weighted-sum evidence scoring Score(E)=sum(w_i) can be invalid under dependent evidence, requiring an explicit dependency model P(E1..En); retrieval selection bias means RetrievedSample≠RepresentativeSample of the true relevant population D* without a sampling argument; ranking is itself a sampling mechanism creating the feedback loop Ranking->Exposure->HumanSelection->EvidenceUse->Knowledge, making retrieval governance part of the epistemic architecture; position bias (Rank->ProbabilityOfInspection) is a recognized system effect, not necessarily undesirable but not neutral either.

anchor: Q' != Q necessarily [after query expansion]. ... Interpret(Q) = {I_1,...,I_n} ... Ambiguous != Resolved. ... RC = <Question,Scope,Sources,TimeWindow,...>
statement: 20.37-20.40: query expansion Q->Q' (synonyms, related concepts, entity resolution, inferred terms) need not preserve Q's intended semantics (Q'≠Q necessarily), risking retrieval drift; some query interpretation is itself inferential (e.g. 'why did sales increase?' admits descriptive/causal/attribution/comparative readings) so Interpret(Q) may need to return a set {I1..In} rather than silently picking one as though true, following Unknown≠False and Ambiguous≠Resolved; formalizes a Retrieval Contract RC=<Question,Scope,Sources,TimeWindow,RetrievalMethods,RankingMethod,Filters,MinimumRecall,MinimumPrecision,Freshness,ProvenanceRequirements> defining what constitutes adequate retrieval, analogous to earlier statistical/causal contracts.

anchor: Delta_R = {r in Req(RC): not Sat(K,r)} ... Zero_R(K,RC) iff Delta_R = empty ... != Truth ... NotRetrieved != Nonexistent ... NoResult [does not imply] False(Q) ... RetrievalProbability != TruthProbability
statement: 20.41-20.48: defines a retrieval knowledge gap Delta_R (source coverage unknown, temporal coverage incomplete, provenance missing, inaccessible documents, unvalidated ranking, unknown recall, unresolved contradictions) and Retrieval Zero Zero_R(K,RC) iff Delta_R=∅, meaning only that the explicit retrieval contract is satisfied -- not that all real-world relevant information was found, nor truth, nor a correct final answer (Zero_R≠Truth); retrieval completeness Rel(Q)⊆Ret(Q) is generally unknown in practice and estimated against Rel*(Q); KnowledgeOS defaults to an open-world assumption unless the contract states otherwise, so NotRetrieved≠Nonexistent (absence may reflect retrieval failure/inaccessible source/indexing failure/ranking exclusion/query formulation, not nonexistence), while a closed-world universe is a contract property, not a universal default; an empty result R=∅ means NoResult under the configuration, not automatically False(Q) or Unknown(Q); retrieval failure (source/index/query/permission/embedding/timeout/ranking failure) must be represented as an operational RetrievalFailure state, not NoEvidenceExists; a retrieval confidence estimate P(Rel|Q,x) is a model output distinct from P(Truth(x)|Q) (RetrievalProbability≠TruthProbability).

anchor: A = G(Q,E,M) [may contain] hallucinations. ... Claim_i -> EvidenceSet_i -> SourceSet_i. ... U(A,E,Gamma) = {c_i: not Supported(c_i,E,Gamma)}
statement: 20.49-20.51: an answer A=G(Q,E,M) generated from question/evidence/model may contain direct quotations, paraphrases, deductions, interpolations, assumptions or hallucinations, so answer generation must preserve claim-level provenance; recommends representing Answer={Claim1..Claimn} with each Claim_i->EvidenceSet_i->SourceSet_i (rather than one source list for an indivisible text) enabling claim-level verification, contradiction detection, and unsupported-claim detection; formalizes unsupported claims U(A,E,Gamma)={c_i: ¬Supported(c_i,E,Gamma)} which a well-governed process should expose rather than silently presenting as established.

anchor: Ret != Infer. ... AI-generated retrieval queries are CandidateQuery ... AI-generated conclusions are CandidateInference.
statement: 20.52-20.54: inference after retrieval E-I->C requires premises/rules/models/assumptions/scope/uncertainty, giving the pipeline Query->Retrieval->EvidenceEvaluation->Inference->Determination and the formal boundary Ret(K,Q)->E followed by Infer(E,Q,Gamma)->C, hence Ret≠Infer, a distinction that should stay visible in the domain model and APIs; an AI system acting as both retriever and generator gains no automatic epistemic authority from either role -- its outputs are labeled CandidateQuery, CandidateEvaluation, CandidateInference pending validation.

anchor: Semantic inflation occurs when a generated representation is assigned a stronger epistemic category than its supporting evidence and contract justify. ... Association -> Causation ... Prediction -> Observation ... Hypothesis -> Determination. ... RetrieverOutput requires provenance verification.
statement: 20.55-20.57: defines hallucination precisely as semantic inflation -- assigning a generated representation a stronger epistemic category than its evidence/contract justify, illustrated by Association->Causation, Prediction->Observation, Hypothesis->Determination -- 'often a failure of semantic control'; notes retrieval itself can hallucinate (nonexistent documents, incorrect source metadata, wrong chunk boundaries, incorrect source associations, fabricated citations), so RetrieverOutput requires provenance verification; proposes citation-integrity conditions Exists(s), Accessible(s), IdentityCorrect(c,s), Supports(s,p), TemporalFit(s,Q), ScopeFit(s,Q) that must all hold before citation confidence should increase.

anchor: The retrieval layer should preserve both [E1|=p and E2|=not p]. It should not automatically resolve p versus not p. ... Fresh != True. ... Authority != Truth. ... DiverseSources != IndependentEvidence.
statement: 20.58-20.62: when retrieval returns conflicting evidence (E1⊨p, E2⊨¬p) the retrieval layer must preserve both rather than auto-resolving, per Retrieval->ConflictPreservation->Evaluation; retrieval must distinguish Relevant from CurrentlyValid (an old source can be highly relevant for historical questions but temporally invalid for current ones), needing TemporalRelevance(Q) in the retrieval contract when applicable; Freshness Fresh(x,t,tau) iff t-t_source(x)≤tau does not imply accuracy (Fresh≠True, a recent incorrect source remains incorrect); authority-based filtering (Authority(s)≥a0) increases admissibility, not truth (Authority≠Truth), preserving the governance/epistemology distinction; a diversity requirement Diversity(E)≥d0 reduces single-source-family dependence but DiverseSources≠IndependentEvidence -- provenance analysis remains necessary.

anchor: RetrievalSystem can be treated as a measurement process over an information universe. ... FalsePositive = R(Q)\R*(Q) ... RelevanceProbability != TruthProbability.
statement: 20.63-20.66: frames retrieval as an epistemic instrument/measurement process (evaluable for sensitivity, specificity, recall, precision, calibration, robustness, bias, coverage), paralleling measurement theory; defines retrieval measurement error via FalsePositive=R(Q)\R*(Q) and FalseNegative=R*(Q)\R(Q) against an ideal relevant set R*(Q), noting these are retrieval errors, not automatically epistemic falsehoods in the retrieved objects; retrieval calibration (does P(Rel|p-hat≈c)≈c hold) is a statistical property of the retrieval model and must not be read as P(Truth|p-hat=c) (RelevanceProbability≠TruthProbability); a model-inferred query expansion Q->Q' that is not semantically equivalent to Q risks answering a different question, so both OriginalQuery and TransformedQuery should be retained with provenance.

anchor: RO = <Question,Query,QueryTransformation,Retriever,RetrieverVersion,Corpus,Index,...> ... ERO = <EvidenceCandidate,RetrievalOperation,Relevance,...> ... Promote(r,EC_E) only if SourceValid and ScopeValid and TemporalValid and ProvenanceValid and EvidenceRequirementsSatisfied.
statement: 20.67-20.70: proposes a 15-field auditable Retrieval Pipeline Object RO=<Question,Query,QueryTransformation,Retriever,RetrieverVersion,Corpus,Index,Filters,Ranking,Results,Selection,Timestamp,Context,Contract,Provenance> and a 9-field Evidence Retrieval Object ERO=<EvidenceCandidate,RetrievalOperation,Relevance,Source,TemporalValidity,Authority,Dependency,SelectionStatus,Provenance> separating candidate retrieval from evidence acceptance; gates the RetrievedObject->Evidence promotion via Promote(r,EC_E) requiring SourceValid∧ScopeValid∧TemporalValid∧ProvenanceValid∧EvidenceRequirementsSatisfied (a semantic transition that 'must not be hidden inside the search engine'); the full pipeline becomes Search->Candidate->Evidence->Premise->Inference->Conclusion, each arrow carrying its own contract.

anchor: Delta_{t+1} superset Delta_t [after rigorous retrieval reveals missing information] ... GapIncrease ⇏ KnowledgeQualityDecrease. ... Complete(R,Q_1,Gamma_1) [does not imply] Complete(R,Q_2,Gamma_2).
statement: 20.71-20.73: retrieval can shrink the knowledge gap (Delta_{t+1}⊆Delta_t) or expose previously-invisible missing information, growing it (Delta_{t+1}⊃Delta_t, e.g. discovering 'no sufficiently authoritative source exists'), which is not failure but improved epistemic awareness -- worked example Delta_0=∅ (requirements unknown) -> Delta_1={r1,r2,r3} after rigorous retrieval, giving GapIncrease⇏KnowledgeQualityDecrease, explicitly said to follow from 'the learning theory of Part XVII'; retrieval completeness is contextual -- Complete(R,Q1,Gamma1) does not transfer to Complete(R,Q2,Gamma2), so 'the knowledge base has been completely searched' has no universal meaning without a target/scope/contract.

lineage_claims.quote: This follows directly from the learning theory of Part XVII.

anchor: Index != CanonicalKnowledgeState. ... Rebuild(K) -> I' ... Sem(I') ≡_Q Sem(I) ... I_t not≈ f(K_t) [index drift]

statement: 21.1: opens Part XXI at the question of how KnowledgeOS constructs and verifies conclusions from premises/rules/models/assumptions/constraints/context without silently promoting a generated conclusion into truth or authority; states the boxed foundational separation Inference≠Reasoning≠Proof≠Determination, with Proof⇏Determination unless the contract treats the proof as sufficient, and Determination⇏Truth unless a soundness bridge to target semantics exists; frames the reasoning engine as a controlled derivation system, not an oracle.

anchor: Definition 21.1 — Inference ... P |-_{rho,Gamma} q ... Definition 21.2 — Reasoning ... R: (K,Gamma) -> D ... Definition 21.3 — Proof ... pi = <q,S,P,A,R,D,V,Prov,Status> ... Definition 21.4 — Determination ... Det(K,q,EC,Gamma) iff for all r in Req_q(EC,Gamma): Sat(K,r) = Satisfied.
statement: 21.2: gives four formal definitions -- Inference I=(P,q,rho,Gamma) with P⊢_{rho,Gamma}q meaning the inference is licensed by rho under Gamma; Reasoning as the controlled process R:(K,Gamma)->D (D = candidate derivations/proofs/failures/conflicts/unresolved states) comprising 10 listed sub-activities, explicitly a process versus inference's semantic relation; Proof as a 9-field structured epistemic artifact pi=<q,S,P,A,R,D,V,Prov,Status>, not a textual explanation; Determination Det(K,q,EC,Gamma) holding iff every requirement in Req_q(EC,Gamma) is satisfied, with reasoning contributing to but not replacing the determination contract.

anchor: Gamma_R = <Context,Time,Contract,Model,Rules,Assumptions,Authority,Resources> ... P |-_{rho,Gamma_1} q [does not imply] P |-_{rho,Gamma_2} q ... A conclusion is always a conclusion under some reasoning semantics.
statement: 21.3-21.4: formalizes the reasoning context as an 8-field tuple Gamma_R=<Context,Time,Contract,Model,Rules,Assumptions,Authority,Resources>, each component potentially changing the result, so P⊢_{rho,Gamma1}q does not transfer to Gamma2 (not necessarily a contradiction, just different reasoning contexts) -- 'a conclusion is always a conclusion under some reasoning semantics'; formalizes a rule as an 8-field tuple rho=<Premises,Conclusion,Conditions,Exceptions,Logic,Authority,Version,Provenance> deliberately preventing 'if X then Y' from being treated as universally valid knowledge, since a rule may be syntactically valid, logically valid, empirically supported, domain-authorized or contract-authorized without satisfying all simultaneously.

anchor: p = <Proposition,Evidence,Status,Scope,Time,Provenance> ... Premise(p) not-equiv Text(p). ... Assumption Dependency Principle ... Impact(a) = {q: a in Dependencies(q)}.
statement: 21.5-21.6: formalizes a premise as p=<Proposition,Evidence,Status,Scope,Time,Provenance>, so Premise(p)≢Text(p) (text expresses but does not establish epistemic status); formalizes reasoning-with-assumptions as P,A⊢q (never collapsed to P⊢q), with the Assumption Dependency Principle stating that if P,A⊢q and a∈A then q is potentially affected by revision of a, enabling Impact(a)={q: a∈Dependencies(q)} for dependency-local revision rather than indiscriminate global invalidation.

anchor: A sound reasoning system satisfies Gamma |- q => Gamma |= q. ... Sound inference != True premises != True conclusion in reality. ... A reasoning calculus is complete ... iff Gamma |= q => Gamma |- q.
statement: 21.7-21.9: Definition 21.5 Soundness -- Gamma⊢q⇒Gamma⊨q, meaning the system derives no semantically invalid conclusions under the specified semantics, explicitly not meaning premises are true / observations correct / model describes reality / data unbiased / contract appropriate (Sound inference≠True premises≠True conclusion in reality); Definition 21.6 Completeness -- Gamma⊨q⇒Gamma⊢q; soundness concerns what is derived, completeness what can be derived, neither guarantees feasibility (a system can be sound+complete but expensive, sound but incomplete, or heuristic and neither) -- KnowledgeOS must store claimed reasoning guarantees explicitly.

anchor: Bird(x) => Flies(x) ... Penguin(x) => not Flies(x) ... K |-_d q [does not imply] K union K' |-_d q. ... Knowledge Evolution != Monotonic Accumulation. ... Induction != Deduction. ... E ~~> H [but] E ⇏ H.
statement: 21.10-21.13: defeasible reasoning (Tweety/penguin example) is generally non-monotonic -- K⊢_d q does not imply K∪K'⊢_d q, aligning with Knowledge Evolution≠Monotonic Accumulation; strict (⊢_s q), defeasible (⊢_d q), heuristic, statistical and abductive conclusions must never collapse into a generic confidence=0.87 field since each has different semantic status; inductive reasoning D↝H must not be read as deductive entailment (Induction≠Deduction), depending on sampling/model-assumptions/estimator/uncertainty/representativeness/bias/model-selection/validation; abductive reasoning E↝H from H⇒E and E does not give E⇒H, so multiple explanatory hypotheses H1..Hn must be preserved rather than one silently selected as truth, even though they may be ranked by explanatory adequacy/simplicity/prior plausibility/predictive performance/causal compatibility/evidence support (ranking does not establish truth).

anchor: F = {x in X: for all c_i in C, c_i(x)=true}. ... F=empty does not mean that a domain proposition is false. ... x* = argmin_{x in F} f(x) ... Optimal(x) ⇏ Authorized(x) [nor] ⇏ True(x). ... Optimal != Authorized != Executed.
statement: 21.14-21.16: defines the feasible set F={x∈X: all c_i∈C hold} with three fundamental cases (Feasible F≠∅, Unique |F|=1, Inconsistent F=∅), stressing F=∅ means the constraint system has no feasible solution, not that a domain proposition is false; unsatisfiability diagnosis via a minimal inconsistent subset C'⊆C requires 'minimal' to have a defined ordering/cost function, never left implicit; optimization-based reasoning x*=argmin_{x∈F}f(x) gives Optimal(x)⇏Authorized(x) and Optimal(x)⇏True(x), explicitly preserving the Part XVI boundary Optimal≠Authorized≠Executed.

anchor: P* = T_R(P*) [fixed point] ... Forward and backward chaining are generally search strategies, not necessarily different epistemic semantics. ... Applicable(rho,K,Gamma) [8 conditions before] Apply(rho,P,Gamma) -> q.
statement: 21.17-21.19: forward chaining repeatedly applies rules P0->P1->P2->... to a fixed point P*=T_R(P*) under the rule-generated consequence operator T_R; backward chaining works from a query q asking which rules could establish it (q<-p1,...,pn), and forward/backward chaining are framed as search strategies rather than distinct epistemic semantics (equivalent results if implementing the same sound calculus); a rule must not fire merely because its text appears applicable -- Applicable(rho,K,Gamma) requires 8 checks (premise availability, type compatibility, temporal validity, contextual validity, authority validity, exception conditions, contract compatibility, rule-version validity) before Apply(rho,P,Gamma)->q, 'a critical architectural safeguard'.

anchor: Conflict = <q,Support(q),Support(not q),Rules,Context,Provenance>. ... KnowledgeOS must never infer priority merely from rule order, database insertion order, textual position, model confidence, or retrieval ranking.
statement: 21.20-21.21: when rules r1:P⇒q and r2:P⇒¬q both fire, the engine must not infer arbitrary x (violating non-explosion q,¬q⊬x) but instead produce an explicit Conflict=<q,Support(q),Support(¬q),Rules,Context,Provenance> object; rule priority r1≻r2 is itself a semantic object requiring a PriorityPolicy=<Scope,Ordering,Authority,Version,Provenance>, and must never be inferred merely from rule storage order, insertion order, textual position, model confidence, or retrieval ranking.

anchor: pi = <Conclusion,Steps,Premises,Rules,Assumptions,Dependencies,Context,Versions,Provenance> ... s_i = <Input,Rule,Output,Context,Status>. ... Cycles are invalid for a proof object unless the declared formalism explicitly defines and verifies their semantics.
statement: 21.22-21.24: formalizes a machine-readable proof object pi=<Conclusion,Steps,Premises,Rules,Assumptions,Dependencies,Context,Versions,Provenance> with each typed proof step s_i=<Input,Rule,Output,Context,Status>; simple derivations are trees (giving premise/rule traceability, dependency visibility, proof checking, impact analysis), but shared premises make a directed acyclic graph D=(V,E) more appropriate, admitting a TopologicalOrder(D) when grounded and acyclic; states the general rule that cycles are invalid for a proof object unless the declared formalism explicitly defines and verifies their semantics (some formalisms permit recursive definitions/cyclic proofs/coinduction/fixed-point semantics).

anchor: Grounded(q) [distinct from] CircularlySupported(q). ... Grounding Principle ... Dependencies(q) = {p,a}. ... Affected(a) = {x: a in Dep*(x)}.
statement: 21.25-21.27: distinguishes Grounded(q) from CircularlySupported(q) -- a circular dependency (p⇒q, q⇒p) is not automatically a valid proof; the Grounding Principle requires a proof to terminate in accepted premises/authorized axioms/validated observations/explicit assumptions/another formally authorized foundation; assumption tracking records Dependencies(q)={p,a} so a later retraction of a yields Affected(q)={q: a∈Dependencies(q)}, generalized via transitive dependency closure Dep*(x) to Affected(a)={x: a∈Dep*(x)}, creating a formal bridge between reasoning, provenance, revision and impact analysis.

statement: 21.39-21.41: the logical closure Cl_L(K) (derivable consequences) is distinct from K itself (explicit epistemic objects), further split into semantic closure (what follows under formal semantics) vs materialized closure (what has actually been computed/stored), so a query failing against materialized closure does not mean NotDerivable(q); for a monotone consequence operator a fixed point K*=T(K*) can represent closure, but this does not transfer to non-monotonic/defeasible systems (K⊆K' does not guarantee Cl(K)⊆Cl(K')), so fixed-point semantics must be explicitly declared; termination is distinct from soundness and completeness (a system can be sound-but-non-terminating, terminating-but-incomplete, complete-but-impractical, or all three only for a restricted fragment) -- Soundness≠Completeness≠Termination, and KnowledgeOS must record the actually-implemented fragment's guarantees.

anchor: Theorem 21.1 — Rule Application Soundness ... Theorem 21.2 — Proof Checking Soundness ... Theorem 21.3 — Conflict Locality ... Theorem 21.4 — Failure Non-Falsity ... statement: 21.55-21.62: Part XXI's eight named theorems, five with explicit short proofs. Theorem 21.1 (proved) -- if premises/rule/conditions/exceptions/authorization/execution all hold then P⊢_{rho,Gamma}q is sound relative to L (P⊢q⇒P⊨_L q), deliberately not establishing premises correspond to reality. Theorem 21.2 (proved) -- Check(pi,Gamma)=Valid under a sound checker implies Gamma⊢_L Conclusion(pi), by induction over proof structure. Theorem 21.3 Conflict Locality (proved) -- under a paraconsistent KnowledgeOS logic, K⊢q and K⊢¬q does not give K⊢r for arbitrary unrelated r absent an explicit deriving rule, since the semantics excludes classical explosion q,¬q⊢r. Theorem 21.4 Failure Non-Falsity (proved) -- ReasoningFailure⇏False(q) since none of the listed failure causes logically entail ¬q. Theorem 21.5 Proof Provenance Preservation (proved) -- a provenance-preserving proof (Prov(pi) containing every premise/rule-version/model-version/assumption/context) supports dependency-local revision via Dep*(q) when a dependency changes. Theorem 21.6 AI Derivation Non-Authorization (proved) -- AI(E,Gamma)->D_c gives D_c⇏ProofValid without independent verification, and ProofValid⇏DecisionAuthorized, so AI->Candidate->Verification->Determination->Decision must remain semantically distinct. Theorem 21.7 Constraint Satisfiability Separation (proved) -- F(C)=∅ (unsatisfiability) does not entail False(p) for an arbitrary domain proposition p, since inconsistency and proposition falsity are different semantic objects. Theorem 21.8 Determination Separation (proved) -- Check(pi)=Valid does not by itself establish Det(K,q,EC,Gamma), since determination requires all contract requirements (evidence, temporal, authority, competing-model, uncertainty) satisfied, not merely proof validity.

statement: 21.66-21.69: new evidence can invalidate premises/assumptions/rules/models/derivations/determinations within the cycle Evidence->Reasoning->Conclusion->Determination->Decision->Action->Observation->Revision, but proof objects are historical epistemic artifacts -- a previously valid proof can remain historically valid while its conclusion is no longer currently accepted (HistoricalValidity≠CurrentValidity); reasoning revision changes ProofStatus_t(pi)=Valid to Superseded or Invalidated at t+1 depending on contract, without deleting the old proof; minimal mutation prefers reconsidering only the dependency closure Affected(a) (LocalRevision over GlobalRecomputation), but this is not an unconditional law -- a global rule change may legitimately require broad recomputation, so minimality is itself contract- and dependency-dependent; rule and model governance must track identity/authority/version/provenance/effective-time/scope/approval-status/change-history (rules) and identity/version/training-lineage/validation-status/scope/limitations (models) -- a rule's mere existence in storage never makes it authorized.

statement: 21.70-21.72: proposes a 13-field conceptual ReasoningCase=<Inquiry,Contract,Premises,Rules,Models,Assumptions,Constraints,Derivations,Proofs,Conflicts,Failures,Verification,Determination> as a semantic composition, not necessarily one implementation aggregate (actual boundaries derived from consistency/transaction/ownership/lifecycle/authority/scale); names 8 architectural anti-patterns to avoid: (1) Universal Rule Table (a generic knowledge_rule(source,target,confidence) table loses logic/assumptions/exceptions/authority/version/provenance), (2) Universal Confidence (one number cannot represent probability/evidence-quality/proof-strength/model-uncertainty/retrieval-relevance/epistemic-status), (3) AI Oracle (LLM output cannot automatically become VerifiedKnowledge), (4) Failure Equals False (violates open-world reasoning), (5) Graph Equals Proof, (6) Ranking Equals Truth, (7) Rule Order Equals Authority (storage order is not governance), (8) Proof Equals Decision (a proof establishes at most what the formal contract permits); restates reasoning as a first-class capability in the pipeline Inquiry->Retrieval->Evidence->Reasoning->Verification->Determination->Decision->Authorization->Action->Observation->Learning/Revision.
